title: 2. SQL Injection (A03)
objective: Study-guide review — ICCS423 v2 — L10: Web Security 1 (Injection · Auth · Access Control · Sessions): 2. SQL Injection (A03).

items: Injection = untrusted data sent to an interpreter as part of a command/query
Interpreter cannot tell "data" from "instruction" → attacker controls logic
Affects: SQL, NoSQL, OS commands, LDAP, XPath, ORM-bypass

blocks.text: Injection is the textbook trust-boundary failure: code and data are concatenated, so user data becomes code.

items: In-band (Classic / Union-based) — attacker sees response; uses UNION SELECT to exfiltrate
Inferential (Blind) — no visible output; uses Boolean (AND 1=1) or Time (SLEEP(5)) signals
Out-of-band (OOB) — DNS/HTTP callback when in-band is impossible

blocks.text: ``sql -- Login form: username = ' OR '1'='1' -- SELECT * FROM users WHERE user='' OR '1'='1' --' AND pass='anything' -- WHERE always TRUE → returns first user (often admin) ``

items: Parameterized queries / prepared statements — separates code from data at the driver level
Stored procedures — only safe if no internal EXEC() of concatenated strings
Input validation (allowlist) — defense-in-depth, not primary defense
Least-privilege DB account — no DROP, GRANT, or system table access
WAF + sanitized error messages — last line; never blind-trust WAF

blocks.text: ```python # ❌ Vulnerable query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=" + user_id
# ✅ Safe — psycopg2 (Python) cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=%s", (user_id,))
# ✅ Safe — JDBC (Java) PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id=?"); stmt.setString(1, userId); ```
Real-world: Heartland Payment Systems (2008) — SQLi → 130M cards stolen, ~$140M cost. SQLi was the initial foothold for lateral movement to a packet sniffer on the payment network.
